summary: Intermittent MPLS LDP route rewrite causes VPCE DNS redirect -> control plane misrouted artifact fetches and corrupted range downloads
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 03:14 UTC BrightAI reported intermittent 502/504 errors and corrupted model shard downloads from Redwood Private deployment. Symptoms include failed range-downloads (partial files with checksum mismatch), control-plane heartbeats showing DNS timeouts, and flakey artifact fetches that correlate with brief spikes in end-customer packet loss.

Impact: Customer's private deployment in us-east-1 experiences failed model pulls when autoscaling serving nodes trigger shard fetches. Application-level errors observed in customer's tracing: S3 presigned range 206 responses replaced by 200 HTML error pages or truncated content, causing model load retries and increased latency. The issue affects production traffic for BrightAI (~40 nodes) and causes cascading rollouts to fail.

Environment: BrightAI private deployment (VPC peered into Redwood control plane via VPCE). VPCE endpoint policy present. Customer uses a managed MPLS circuit to their on-prem datacenter which peers into the same transit provider as their egress path.

Observed start: 2026-03-10 03:14 UTC
Observed pattern: Intermittent, correlated with short BGP/LDP flaps reported by the carrier; lasts 10-30s and resolves.
steps_to_reproduce: From BrightAI environment, trigger parallel model artifact range requests (multipart range GETs) to presigned S3 URLs via VPCE while generating sustained outbound traffic through MPLS path
Monitor TCP connection state and DNS responses to api.redwood-inference.internal (control plane hostname) during the window
Reproduce traffic surge that triggers autoscaling on serving nodes to force concurrent shard downloads
logs: 2026-03-10T03:14:12Z control-plane: fetch_artifact presigned_url=*** status=206 size=245760 shard_id=12
2026-03-10T03:14:13Z edge-proxy: range-request-received range=bytes=0-65535 returned=200 content-type=text/html size=4096
2026-03-10T03:14:13Z customer-tcpdump: DNS response for api.redwood-inference.internal -> 10.20.30.5 (internal edge) via MPLS next-hop (unexpected)
2026-03-10T03:14:14Z control-plane: auth handshake delayed tls_resume_retry count=3
comments: Aisha Patel (Support): Initial triage: customer reports corrupted shard files and failed node startups. Requested pcap and DNS traces.
BrightAI Tier1 (customer): Uploaded tcpdump and traceroute; pointed to intermittent route changes to our VPCE prefix originating at the carrier (MPLS).

Connor Lee (SRE): Noted DNS responses we received mid-flap resolved to an internal edge address owned by carrier (10.20.30.5) rather than expected VPCE resolver IP. Hypothesis: MPLS provider injected a deterministic NAT/DNS rewrite during LDP re-convergence.
Connor Lee (SRE): Requested carrier ticket and BGP/LDP logs from BrightAI. Also recommended temporary IP pinning for VPCE in customer's route table as a mitigation.
BrightAI Network Lead: Opened a carrier TAC case; carrier confirmed brief LDP session resets during maintenance window and NAT appliance performed DNS rewrite to a maintenance cache node.
investigation_notes: TCP dump analysis shows that during the event DNS A queries for api.redwood-inference.internal returned a private address (10.20.30.5) for ~12-27s windows; subsequent TLS handshake to that address failed ALPN and returned HTTP/1.1 200 error HTML for range requests.

Traceroute and mpls labels indicate that traffic shifted to a maintenance LSP where an edge cache appliance (carrier-managed) was present. That appliance rewrote DNS answers to point to a maintenance front-end that does not honor S3 presigned range semantics, causing 200 responses with HTML bodies instead of 206 partial content.
Control-plane logs show retry storms as artifact checksum validation failed and retries exhausted, increasing tail latency and triggering additional model reload attempts.
No Redwood control-plane configuration change correlated to the time window. VPCE endpoint policy and prefix lists remained unchanged. The carrier's maintenance was the only external factor.
We reproduced a similar failure in lab by simulating a DNS response rewrite to an alternate IP that serves non-S3 content; artifacts truncated and checksums failed identically.
resolution_notes: Short-term mitigation applied (2026-03-11 01:40 UTC): instructed BrightAI to add static route to their VPC route table pointing VPCE resolver IPs to a preferred IGW path that bypasses MPLS egress for control-plane resolution. This avoided the carrier rewrite and stopped the corrupted downloads.
Applied a temporary VPCE endpoint policy suggestion: require host header validation and strict TLS SNI checks on control-plane hostnames to reject rewritten responses from non-Redwood front-ends.

Carrier root cause: planned MPLS LDP maintenance triggered a failover to a maintenance LSP where a cache appliance returned rewritten DNS responses pointing to maintenance hosts. Carrier to update maintenance playbook to avoid DNS rewrites for customer VPCE prefixes. BrightAI to obtain maintenance exclusion from carrier for our VPCE CIDRs.

Long-term action items: (1) Add detection to Redwood control-plane for mismatched content-types on presigned range responses and fail fast with clearer error to customers; (2) Add guidance in Private Deploy runbook to pin VPCE resolver IPs or use secondary egress path for artifact fetches; (3) Coordinate with carriers to include VPCE CIDRs in maintenance exclusion lists.
Status: customer workaround validated, carrier escalated. Follow-up planned with BrightAI and carrier for closure.
